title: Week 2 Analysis
subtitle: Last week's cellar is this week's penthouse.
intro_paragraphs: Two weeks in, and the leaderboard has almost nothing in common with where it started. The picks didn't change — the standings did, and that was enough to flip the pool upside down.

fun_facts.heading: The Great Reversal
fun_facts.body:
Dilger finished Week 1 in 6th place with 22 points. One week later, Dilger leads the pool at 68 — a 46-point jump, the biggest single-week swing anyone had. Hume did almost the same thing from the other direction: dead last at 20 points after Week 1, now sitting 3rd at 65, a 45-point gain.

Meanwhile Dustin, who led the pool after Week 1 with 40 points, gained only 2 all week and has fallen to 7th. Whatever was working in Week 1 stopped working immediately.

fun_facts.heading: Tight at the Top, a Cliff Underneath
fun_facts.body: First and second are separated by exactly 1 point — Dilger's 68 to Cadegn's 67, the closest gap anywhere on the board. Hume (65) and Tom (64) are right behind them too. Then the board falls off a cliff: 13 points separate Tom in 4th from Mike T in 5th, the widest gap in the pool and the clearest dividing line between this week's contenders and everyone else.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks Are Clawing Back
fun_facts.body:
Five of the eight preseason unanimous picks are holding again, up from just two after Week 1. The Bills-first, Patriots-second read on the AFC East — which the Jets blew up in Week 1 — is back to matching reality, and the Cardinals reclaimed last place in the NFC West right on schedule.

But the pool's single most confident pick still hasn't shown up: the Rams, unanimous choices to win the NFC West, are stuck behind Seattle for a second straight week. Hume currently has the best read on the season overall, with 4 of 8 division-winner picks now sitting in first place; Dustin is still waiting on a second one.

closing_paragraph: Whoever's ahead after two weeks has no real lead on the season — ask Dustin. Next week resets the same way it always does.
